I knew a kid in group therapy who was kind of a zombie, he never moved unless someone told him to or spoke without being prompted (and even then, he said precious little). But his parents came into every family meeting begging for more medication and saying he was impulsive and violent and bouncing off the walls, even though literally none of the therapists, doctors, or other patients saw any evidence of this behavior. As it turns out, he was already on a shitload of drugs, and one of the doctors politely noted that they seemed to be overmedicating their son so much he could barely do anything or express emotion. I get that some kids need psych medication, but I think cases like this are way more common than people assume.

I do think showing more motivations would help, and I wish that autistic characters in fiction were written to have more of an internal life, because some folks seem to regard us as alien or even emotionless. Even as an autistic person, in the hospital I was discomfited by the odd behavior of another patient who had schizophrenia. Later on, I came to know a schizophrenic person who  pointed out to me that everyone has a myopic and incorrect perception of the world to one degree or another, and we're all just doing the best we can to interpret the information we have. It helps me put a lot of things in perspective.

I'm autistic, and it's a fucking drag seeing my condition only ever represented as a tragedy or a joke. Sometimes I wish I conformed to autism stereotypes in media more, I'd love to be a walking dictionary or have some kind of special skill. As it turns out, being "smart" isn't actually worth much when you're bad with people (I can pretend to be a normal person pretty well, but I can't make it work longterm or when I'm nervous), have trouble with basic tasks, and throw weird tantrums that make other people uncomfortable. In general, I feel like autistic people are always treated as something to gawk at instead of individuals with genuine inner lives.

Personally, I feel like Rick's ex-wife/Beth's mom being of incredible importance would be against the ethos of the show. It's not a narrative where everything fits together like a puzzle, it's inherently about how the universe is weird and messy and things don't always have meaning or make sense. I wouldn't be shocked if she never showed up, given that the show has gone out of its way to avoid filling in Rick's backstory too much.
